headline: Cloudflare has released Void as open-source software, giving companies a way to host and control the apps their employees now build with AI.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 4: Cloudflare announced Void on Thursday 15 Oct, before this edition's window.
importance_line: IT teams and security staff at companies that let non-engineers build software with AI are affected first, but the platform leaves security review to each company and runs on Cloudflare's paid services.
summary: The New Stack reports that Cloudflare, the web infrastructure company, announced on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 that Void, a set of three open-source tools, is now fully open source, including a self-hosted platform where companies can deploy employees' AI-built apps while administrators control who can deploy and use them. The report notes limits: administrators can set new apps to be public by default, Void has no mandatory security review before an app goes live, and companies that host the platform themselves need a paid Cloudflare plan, from $25 a month, plus a separately hosted database.
notes: Read The New Stack in full (16 Oct). 'Thursday' is 15 Oct 2026. Cloudflare executives (Michael Dong, strategy lead; Christoph Nakazawa, director of engineering) are quoted directly, hence CONFIRMED. VoidZero was acquired by Cloudflare in June, Deno last week, Astro in January per the article.
